# Task tracker build report

Mission: r1-web-fca8d1ca-5530-4737-b27d-af18c15f5989

## file_list inventory (product/)

| File | Size (bytes) |
|---|---|
| product/index.html | 838 |
| product/styles.css | 2028 |
| product/app.js | 5617 |

The tree has exactly these three files. index.html references only styles.css and app.js, and both exist in product/.

## Requirement checklist (by inspection of file_read output)

**Controls**
- One heading: a single h1 element, Task tracker, in index.html.
- Textbox New task: label for=new-task plus input id=new-task type=text autocomplete=off.
- Button Add task: button type=submit inside form#task-form.
- Combobox Filter tasks: label for=filter plus select#filter with option values all, active, completed (all is the default).
- List Tasks: ul#task-list with aria-label=Tasks, empty in the markup, so zero li elements when storage is empty.
- Each li (buildItem in app.js) holds a span with textContent set to the task text, a checkbox with aria-label Complete plus the text, and a Delete button with aria-label Delete plus the text.

**Behavior**
- Add: the form submit handler calls preventDefault, so the button click and Enter share one path. addTask trims the value; an empty result adds nothing and refocuses the input; success clears the input.
- Literal rendering: text goes only through textContent and setAttribute. There is no innerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML or document.write.
- Toggle: the checkbox change event calls toggleTask, which sets completed to the checkbox state in both directions.
- Filtering: matchesFilter and pruneNonMatching (called on toggle), and render (called on filter change), remove non-matching li nodes from the DOM.
- Persistence: saveStorage writes a JSON array of id, text, completed under awe-task-tracker.v1 after every add, toggle and delete. readStorage wraps storage access and JSON.parse in try/catch and drops malformed entries.
- Ids: an incrementing counter (t1, t2, ...), re-seeded from stored ids on load. There are no crypto APIs.
- Delete: removeTask filters by id, so duplicate texts stay independent.

**Accessibility and layout**
- Native visible controls only; no display:none and no tabindex.
- :focus-visible outline is defined in styles.css.
- box-sizing:border-box is set globally, and .container uses width:100% with max-width:720px.
- The form, filter row and list rows use flex-wrap. Task text, labels and buttons use overflow-wrap:anywhere and word-break:break-word.
- There are no fixed widths larger than the viewport. These layout rules are unmeasured; no browser was available to check 375px or 1280px.

**Network and CSP**
- CSS and JS load only as local relative files (styles.css, app.js defer).
- There are no inline script blocks, inline event handlers, inline style attributes or CSP meta tag.
- There is no fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket, EventSource, worker, iframe, object, embed, web font, CDN link, remote image or favicon.
- No URL literals or protocol-relative references appear in the three files as read back.

**Acceptance (browser errors, console errors, missing resources)**
- The app.js code has no console calls and no throws; DOM lookups are guarded with an early return, and storage access is in try/catch.
- This is by inspection only, since there was no shell or browser.

## Blockers and limits
- No shell tool was granted, so node --check and a real browser run were not possible. The JS uses conservative ES5-style syntax inside an IIFE to suit the independent verifier.
- No verification receipt exists and none is claimed. The independent verifier's result on the exact tree is still pending.
